newsitem.title: INDIA: ITC in spotlight as Bombay shares end flat.
newsitem.headline: ITC in spotlight as Bombay shares end flat.

text.p: Indian tobacco conglomerate ITC Ltd was in the limelight at Bombay exchanges on Monday but other shares ended flat as profit-taking wiped out a sharp early rally, traders said.
The Bombay share index ended 18.05 points higher at 3,777.69, off 3,806.15 --the intra-day high.
"We saw some profit-taking in small cap stocks today, but the markets were led by ITC," said Maulik Sharedalal, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange.
ITC is expected to report sharply higher profits for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) on the back of a robust growth in cigarette sales and improved margins, analysts said on Monday.

"Strong cigarette sales growth, expansion of margins and the possibility of lower write-offs would boost profits," said Sandeep Bhatia, ITC analyst at UBS Securities, the investment arm of Union Bank of Switzerland.
ITC is one of India's top 10 private companies. Britain's BAT Industries Plc holds 31.7 percent equity in ITC.
UBS's Bhatia forecast net profit to jump 41 percent to 3.67 billion rupees as the company benefits from hiving off, or closing down, loss-making ventures.
Profits had fallen to 2.61 billion rupees in 1995/96 from 2.62 billion the previous year, due to loss-making deals in farm products and global trade.
Traders said the market was likely to stay in a small trading band as investors book profits at higher levels.
They said investors have become more selective, focussing on bargain-priced stocks after a spate of company results showed the effects of an economic slowdown and tighter margins.
"Sectors that can be bought at current levels are software and pharmaceuticals," said Girish Desai, head of reseach at Prabhudas Lilladher Pvt Ltd.
"We still remain convinced of the bullishness of the market, which has now spread across a wider range of stocks," brokerage Khandwala Securities said in a report.
Shares of Bajaj Auto ended 3.75 rupees lower at 867.0 after the firm set a bonus share issue of one share for every two shares held.
